question: Can two fixed pure-scene CNH templates explain a partly occluded scene better than either alone, without reporting dual components after foreground removal?
model: signed24-bin y=aB+bF, a,b>=0; pure reference medians from first2 inner seconds; exact two-column nonnegative least squares; no bin removal, interpolation, distance replacement or neural training
errors: E=norm(y-yhat,2)/norm(y,2); both single-template alternatives fit their own nonnegative amplitude; gain=min(E_background,E_foreground)-E_dual is an absolute normalized-error drop
floors: a floor=max(0.1,max a on foreground last2seconds); b floor=max(0.1,max b on background last2seconds); fixed before mixture and return scoring
eligibility: all four one-second blocks present in each phase; pure controls >=80% existing status5 distance>3mm; foreground scalar median below background; background dominant bin at least2 later than foreground; template cosine<=0.95; no selection on mixture or return
scope: all16zones reported; at least one passing zone is a feasibility witness only; many correlated frames/zones do not establish generalization
rgb_gate: review three frames per phase for fixed sensor/background, full-book reference, partial-book mixture at approximately unchanged foreground distance, and clear return; missing or ambiguous execution means NOT_EVALUABLE
limits: Camera field coverage does not prove exact ToF-zone occupancy.
Coefficients are waveform-template amplitudes, not area fractions or object counts.
NNLS improvement alone is insufficient; pure controls and return false-dual gate are required.
Matching two reference shapes does not establish exact distance, physical source uniqueness, optical crosstalk cause or obstacle benefit.
stop: one four-stage capture, no automatic rerecording, bin search, post-outcome threshold change or firmware modification; failed eligibility is NOT_EVALUABLE, failed qualified contrast is NOT_SUPPORTED
